scientific_intent.scientific_task: Update a dense vector with a scaled sparse vector and scaled previous state
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: Y <- beta*Y + alpha*X, where X has unique zero-based sparse indices; repeat20 updates from the same initialized dense state
scientific_intent.discretization: No physical discretization. Three named n4099 cases with1027,4099,7 unique sorted indices; signed dyadic values and alpha/beta=(1,1),(-.5,.5),(2,0).
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: All12297 actual output values checked against independent dense Float64 mathematical recurrence with Float32 rounding after each source stage. All20 model/trial checks pass, numerical maxerror0; all portable arrays agree with both references.
scientific_intent.input_size_regime: Three vectors of4099 elements; sparsity fractions1027/4099,1,7/4099. Twenty recurrent updates per trial. This is a small dispatch-scale named study, not large-vector bandwidth scaling.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float32 value arithmetic with signed dyadic fixtures, Int64 sparse indices, bounded output values. Signed zero is numerically equivalent under the unchanged1e-6 absolute contract; raw bit patterns preserved, no output canonicalization.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Sparse-plus-dense updates occur in numerical linear algebra and iterative algorithms. This benchmark is a primitive, not an implemented Krylov solver or evidence of solver convergence.
scientific_intent.description: Complete sparse AXPBY, including dense beta scaling outside sparse support, sparse accumulation, alpha/beta variants, and repeated-state dependence. Unique indices eliminate conflicting scatter writes without atomics.
scientific_intent.provenance: Native source calls cuSPARSE cusparseAxpby; genuine existing CUDA.jl performs a scale kernel and unique-index scatter kernel. Study preserves both implementations, replaces random source input with an explicit shared fixture, and excludes input reset consistently. No native or CUDA.jl mathematical correction.
